root_cause.text: The instance teardown code cleared the COPY_MARKER flag before calling update_marker_trace(), causing the function to skip the RCU synchronization (`synchronize_rcu()`) needed after removing the trace_array from the RCU-protected `marker_copies` list, allowing a use-after-free when concurrent readers still hold a reference.

tracing: Allow the top level trace_marker to write into another instances

There are applications that have it hard code
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7b382efd5e8af4c0c67e70ad3fb599dcd2dc0b86
Author: Steven Rostedt <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Date:   Thu May 8 09:56:39 2025 -0400

    tracing: Allow the top level trace_marker to write into another instances
    
    There are applications that have it hard coded to write into the top level
    trace_marker instance (/sys/kernel/tracing/trace_marker). This can be
    annoying if a profiler is using that instance for other work, or if it
    needs all writes to go into a new instance.
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the COPY_MARKER feature and in __remove_instance() at line 10012-10013, it correctly calls update_marker_trace(tr, 0) which removes the trace_array from the marker_copies list and clears the flag, and then synchronize_rcu() is called if the removal occurred. This ensures that concurrent RCU readers see the removal before the instance is freed, preventing use-after-free. No vulnerable construct is present.
